fatal_errors: The proposed single-phase CoCrFeMnNi system does not match the as-cast dual-phase FCC+B2 AlCoCrFeNi2.1 alloy.
It replaces intermediate-temperature thermal aging at approximately 600–750 °C with deformation at 150–250 °C, missing the relevant brittle aging window.
It attributes brittleness to grain-boundary segregation rather than L12 ordering, jagged FCC/B2 phase boundaries, elevated APBE, planar slip, and phase-boundary stress concentration.
It predicts a strain-rate-dependent transition rather than the observed non-monotonic ductile-brittle-ductile dependence on aging temperature.

The claim that lower strain rates reduce stress-assisted segregation is kinetically questionable because slower loading generally provides more time for diffusion, absent a separately demonstrated rate-dependent driving force.
No prior evidence is supplied for rapid principal-element segregation during tensile testing at 150–250 °C.
explanation: The response addresses HEA embrittlement and proposes measurements with an explicit falsification rule, but it reconstructs none of the target material, aging treatment, temperature window, structural mediator, mechanism, or ductile-brittle-ductile outcome. APT and microscopy could test the proposed segregation mechanism, although quench-and-APT observations would require careful controls to distinguish deformation-induced segregation from pre-existing or preparation-induced chemistry. The hypothesis is also weakly supported kinetically and lacks cited evidence. It therefore constitutes an unsupported alternative rather than a reconstruction of the reported mechanism.
